## feature

## fix

### Post-commit failures still deleted published outputs

```
level: high
```

#### reason

High: data loss. The batch-3 commit point was comment-only — after the
last publication, exceptions from `input_file.close()` or the
TemporaryDirectory cleanup still reached the rollback handlers, which
deleted every published output.

#### description

```
type: text
```

1. An explicit `committed` flag is set immediately after the last
   publication.
2. When committed, every exception handler skips rollback entirely,
   prints a post-commit warning (outputs kept), and re-raises; an OSError
   becomes an `OutputError` naming the post-commit state.
3. Pre-commit failures keep the full backup/restore rollback, unchanged
   and regression-tested.

#### before

```text
second run (cleanup failure after publication) exit=1
files after: []
```

#### after

```text
second run (cleanup failure after publication) exit=1
files after: ['a.bam', 'd.parquet', 's.parquet']
pairmerge: warning: failure after publication; all outputs were already
           published and are kept (no rollback).
```

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Regression: `tests/test_errors.py::TestPublishIntegrity::test_post_commit_failure_keeps_published_outputs`
(one-shot `TemporaryDirectory.cleanup` failure; asserts exit 1, all
outputs present, and the post-commit messages on stderr). The batch-3
publish-restore and cleanup-litter tests still pass.
:::

### Colocated mates received same-sign TLEN

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: invalid metadata per the SAM spec — TLEN signs must be opposite
within a template even when both segments cover identical coordinates,
and a first-party test pinned the invalid value.

#### description

```
type: text
```

`_sync_mate_fields` assigns `(tlen, -tlen)` on equal starts: read1 takes
the positive sign, per the SAM TLEN tie rule (SAMv1 §1.4.1). The
`(400,400)` integration-test expectation changed from both-positive to
`(+16, -16)`.

#### before

```text
flag=67 pos=500 tlen=20
flag=179 pos=500 tlen=20
```

#### after

```text
flag=67 pos=500 tlen=20
flag=179 pos=500 tlen=-20
```

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Regression: `tests/test_integration.py::TestPairAwareOptimization::test_colocated_mates_tlen_signs`;
updated expectation in `test_joint_overlap_maximization` (read2 now
`-16`).
:::

### Mixed paired/unpaired validation depended on record order

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: silent record loss for one ordering of an invalid template — the
unpaired primary was overwritten in the processing slot when it came
first.

#### description

```
type: text
```

`process_template` validates the primary group as a whole before
assigning slots: mixed paired/unpaired primaries raise regardless of
order, and more than one unpaired primary raises explicitly (previously
misreported as a mix).

#### before

```text
order [0, 65] (unpaired first) exit=0  <- silently accepts
order [65, 0] (paired first) exit=1    <- correctly rejects
```

#### after

```text
order [0, 65] exit=1 (same DataInvariantError both ways)
order [65, 0] exit=1
```

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Regressions: `tests/test_classify_policy.py::TestRecordPolicy::test_mixed_paired_unpaired_rejected_in_any_order`,
`test_two_unpaired_primaries_rejected`.
:::

## caveat

### Post-commit failures exit 1 with complete outputs

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

Medium: a two-tier post-commit contract is now documented behavior;
downstream automation must not assume exit 1 implies missing outputs.

#### description

```
type: text
```

After the commit point: backup-removal litter warns and exits 0; any
other failure warns, exits 1, and leaves every published output in place.
The error message names the post-commit state explicitly.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: text
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
Pinned by the post-commit regression test and stated in the README
failure-policy section.
:::
